issues.t: Water pump and thermostat coolant leaks
issues.sym: Coolant drips under the car, a sweet smell, a low-coolant or high-temperature warning, or a gauge that runs hot.
issues.why: The water pump is the most-reported problem on the Clubman in TrueDelta's owner survey, followed by the thermostat and its plastic housing. They leak or fail as the car ages.
issues.next: Watch the coolant level and stop if the engine overheats. A shop can pressure-test the system; many owners replace the pump and thermostat together.

issues.t: Timing chain rattle on cold start
issues.sym: A loud rattle for a few seconds after a cold start, sometimes called the death rattle. A check engine light may follow.
issues.why: A weak timing chain tensioner lets the chain go slack and slap its plastic guides, and the chain stretches. Timing chain parts are among the most-reported Clubman repairs.
issues.next: Get it checked right away; a chain that jumps a tooth can wreck the engine. Fresh oil and a new tensioner help early, but a stretched chain and guides need replacing.

issues.t: High-pressure fuel pump failure
issues.sym: On-and-off loss of power, a check engine light, then hard starting or limp mode.
issues.why: The turbo engine's direct-injection fuel pump is a known failure item on second-generation MINIs, including the Clubman's Cooper S engine.
issues.next: Have the fuel pressure codes read. A failing pump needs replacing; check whether your car got the extended warranty coverage MINI offered on some pumps.

issues.t: Carbon buildup on intake valves
issues.sym: Hesitation, lost power, a rough idle or misfire codes, often from 20,000-30,000 miles on.
issues.why: With direct injection, fuel no longer washes the intake valves, so oily vapor bakes on as carbon and restricts airflow.
issues.next: Ask a MINI specialist about an intake valve cleaning (walnut blasting). Good-quality oil and regular highway driving slow the buildup.

issues.t: Turbo oil feed line leak
issues.sym: Oil drips or smoke near the turbo, a burning oil smell, or in bad cases a whining or failing turbo.
issues.why: The pipe that feeds oil to the turbo leaks at its joints and can clog with baked oil on high-mileage cars, starving the turbo.
issues.next: Have the line replaced when it starts leaking; it is much cheaper than a new turbo.

issues.t: Valve cover and oil pan gasket leaks
issues.sym: Oil seeping around the top of the engine or spark plug area, drips under the car, or a burning oil smell.
issues.why: The rocker (valve) cover gasket and oil pan gasket harden with age. Oil leaks from engine gaskets are common Clubman complaints.
issues.next: Keep the oil topped up and have the leaking gasket replaced before oil soaks belts or coils.

issues.t: Misfires from failing ignition coils
issues.sym: A shaking idle, stumbling acceleration and a flashing or steady check engine light.
issues.why: Ignition coil packs are a regular repair on the Clubman according to owner surveys, and worn spark plugs speed up coil failure.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read. Replacing the bad coil and the spark plugs together usually fixes it.

issues.t: Power steering pump failure
issues.sym: The steering suddenly gets heavy, a power steering warning appears, or the pump whines.
issues.why: These Clubmans use an electric motor to drive the power steering pump, and RepairPal notes the pump is prone to failure.
issues.next: Have it checked soon; steering without assist takes much more effort. The pump and fan are usually replaced as one unit.

issues.t: Engine stalling when warm
issues.sym: The engine stalls when warm, often when coming to a stop.
issues.why: RepairPal lists warm stalling as a reported Clubman problem. Sensor, fuel and idle-control faults are common causes on these engines.
issues.next: Have the stored codes read while the problem is fresh. Note when it happens to help the shop find it.

issues.t: Footwell module water damage fire risk (recall)
issues.sym: Wet carpet in the driver's footwell, or lights, windows or other electrics acting strangely.
issues.why: Water and road salt can reach the footwell control module, corrode it and short it out, which could start a fire. Recall 23V-337 covers cars in road-salt states.
issues.next: Run your VIN for open recalls. Dealers check the sunroof drains and module and replace parts free of charge.

issues.t: Turbo coolant pump fire risk (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke from the engine bay, or a coolant warning.
issues.why: The electric pump that cools the turbo after shutdown has a circuit board that can overheat and smolder. Recalls 12V-008 and 18V-248.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the pump replaced free. Until it is done, MINI advised parking outside.

issues.t: ABS warning symbol incomplete (recall)
issues.sym: The ABS warning light shows only a circle without the letters ABS.
issues.why: A small number of 2011 cars got a European-spec tachometer whose ABS symbol does not meet U.S. rules, so a fault could be missed. Recall 11V-299.
issues.next: Dealers already fixed affected cars; a VIN check confirms it.

issues.t: Cracked oil filter housing (2.0L turbo)
issues.sym: Oil or coolant leaking around the engine, low coolant, or the two fluids mixing.
issues.why: The oil filter housing on BMW's 2.0L turbo engine can crack. It sits under the intake manifold, so the repair is labor-heavy. A 2017 Clubman owner reported this exact failure to NHTSA.
issues.next: Have any coolant or oil leak looked at soon. Running low on coolant can overheat the engine.

issues.t: Electric water pump or coolant hose failure (2.0L turbo)
issues.sym: Coolant leaking under the car, an overheating warning, or a car that leaves you stranded.
issues.why: The electric water pump and plastic coolant return hoses on the 2.0L turbo engine are known to fail and leak.
issues.next: Check under the car for coolant and watch the temperature. If a coolant warning appears, stop and get it towed rather than driving hot.

issues.t: Secure vehicle warning from gear selector spring
issues.sym: After shifting to Park, the dash says P not engaged and tells you to secure the car with the parking brake.
issues.why: A small return spring in the automatic shifter breaks, so the car cannot tell it is in Park. MINI extended coverage on this part to 10 years or 120,000 miles.
issues.next: Set the parking brake every time until it is fixed. Ask a MINI dealer about the extended warranty, and request reimbursement if you already paid.

issues.t: Rear brake lights failing or melting
issues.sym: A brake light warning, brake lights that do not work, or a melted lamp socket.
issues.why: Several 2017 owners told NHTSA their rear brake lights failed, shorted or melted.
issues.next: Check your brake lights often and have a failed lamp or socket fixed right away, since other drivers may not see you stop.

issues.t: Inner brake lights switch off with turn signal (recall)
issues.sym: The inner rear brake light goes out when braking with a turn signal on.
issues.why: The lighting software needs reprogramming. Recall 17V-222.
issues.next: Have the dealer reprogram the lights free of charge.

issues.t: Side curtain airbags may not deploy properly (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign.
issues.why: The front side curtain airbags may not deploy where they should, failing the ejection-protection standard. Recall 16V-553.
issues.next: Have the dealer modify the airbag covers free of charge.

issues.t: Driver seat belt may not lock (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign; the belt may not lock in a crash.
issues.why: The locking mechanism in the driver's seat belt may not work as designed. Recall 16V-747.
issues.next: Have the driver's belt replaced free of charge.

issues.t: Seat side airbags may not deploy (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign.
issues.why: The igniter in the seat-mounted side airbag may not fire in a crash. Recall 16V-914.
issues.next: Have the airbag modules replaced free of charge.

issues.t: Engine stalling from crankshaft sensor (recall)
issues.sym: The engine shuts off while driving.
issues.why: The crankshaft sensor may have the wrong software and misread engine position. Recall 18V-465.
issues.next: Have the dealer replace the sensor free of charge.

issues.t: Head airbags may not fire in a rollover (recall)
issues.sym: An airbag warning light may come on.
issues.why: A rollover sensor fault in the airbag control unit could keep the head airbags and belt pretensioners from firing. Recall 20V-283, Cooper S ALL4.
issues.next: Have the airbag control unit replaced free of charge.

issues.t: Passenger seat belt locking feature may release early (recall)
issues.sym: A passenger belt pulled out to hold a child seat does not stay locked.
issues.why: The automatic locking retractor may switch off before the belt fully retracts. Recall 21V-554.
issues.next: Have the dealer inspect and replace the retractor if needed.
